$comment: MCP tool contract for hubmcp (backend/cmd/hubmcp). Frozen; edit only via a CCR to contract-steward. JSON Schemas are 2020-12. See README.md in this folder.

server.name: hubmcp
server.title: Integration Hub
server.description: Lets an AI assistant discover and call Integration Hub integrations as a tenant and, with the signed-in user's own admin token, read operational state and create or change what a team needs on the control plane (never delete).

env.name: HUB_BASE_URL
env.description: Base URL of the Hub gateway, e.g. http://localhost:8080. The admin API is reached at HUB_ADMIN_BASE_URL or, if unset, HUB_BASE_URL with /admin/v1.

env.name: HUB_API_KEY
env.description: Tenant API key (scope `invoke`; add `dry_run` to enable hub_dry_run). Sent as `Authorization: Bearer`. Never logged or echoed. Required unless the ISFC credential (HUB_ISFC_CLIENT_ID + HUB_ISFC_API_KEY) is set; setting both is a startup error.

env.name: HUB_ISFC_CLIENT_ID
env.description: Id of the ISFC backend client that owns HUB_ISFC_API_KEY. Sent as `x-isfc-client-id` on tenant tools. Set together with HUB_ISFC_API_KEY.

env.name: HUB_ISFC_API_KEY
env.description: ISFC API key issued by the integration-hub client to HUB_ISFC_CLIENT_ID. Sent as `x-isfc-api-key` on tenant tools instead of HUB_API_KEY. This is the credential for the streamable-http transport, where one shared server acts for a backend client rather than a signed-in user. Never logged or echoed.

env.name: HUB_TENANT_ID
env.description: ISFC tenant UUID. Sent as `X-Tenant-Id` on tenant tools when the ISFC credential covers more than one tenant (the Hub answers 400 without it), and on hub_admin_* calls to pick the ISFC tenant the signed-in user acts in. Ignored with HUB_API_KEY, which belongs to one tenant.

env.name: HUB_ADMIN_TOKEN
env.description: The signed-in user's own access token (the OIDC token, or in ISFC mode the user's ISFC JWT; locally `hubctl login -dev`), never a shared or service token. When unset, no hub_admin_* tool is registered. Admin read tools follow the existing transport rule; admin write tools are registered only on stdio. The Hub's RBAC (x-required-role, x-required-permission) decides what the user may do.

env.name: HUB_ADMIN_BASE_URL
env.description: Override for the control-plane base URL. Locally e.g. http://localhost:8081/admin/v1. In ISFC mode it is the ISFC api-gateway route to the Hub admin API (the admin listener accepts only gateway traffic), e.g. https://gateway.example.com/integration-hub/admin/v1; the gateway authenticates the user's token and adds the identity headers.

rules: Tenant tools (no `hub_admin_` prefix) MUST NOT reveal vendor names, account names, integration versions or transformer versions. The server strips the X-Hub-Integration-Version header and never puts it in tool output. A pass-through result (pass_through=true: the integration has no response transformer) is the third party's body exactly as the Hub returned it; hubmcp does not alter it.
The only exception is hub_dry_run, which returns the upstream request shape (secrets redacted) by design. Its description says so.

hub_invoke MUST refuse (without calling the Hub) when the integration has moves_money_or_quota=true and the input lacks confirm=true or idempotency_key. The server checks the flag via getIntegration before every such invoke (cached ≤ 60 s).
Admin read tools (readOnlyHint=true) call only GET operations or the non-mutating POST checks (validate, run goldens, transformer dry-run). They never unseal.

Admin write tools (readOnlyHint=false) act as the signed-in user with that user's own HUB_ADMIN_TOKEN and are registered only on the stdio transport, never on streamable-http (a token there would serve every client). The Hub's RBAC (x-required-role) is the authority; FORBIDDEN comes back as an isError result.

No tool maps to an HTTP DELETE or to any operation in forbidden_operations (deletes, purge, replay, unseal, account lifecycle, credential and signing-secret operations, breaker force, pause and resume, key revoke and rotate). Destructive actions stay manual in the console for people whose role allows them. Every hub-admin operation is listed exactly once: mapped by a tool, in forbidden_operations, or in not_exposed_operations.

No admin tool input has a property named in forbidden_input_properties, and no mutating admin tool input has one named in forbidden_mutation_input_properties. Credentials and signing secrets are set in the console or with hubctl, never through an LLM.

Every mutating admin tool requires reason (3-1000 characters). hubmcp sends it with ' (via hubmcp)' appended, so the change log shows who (the token subject), why, and that the change came through MCP.

A tool with requires_confirm refuses locally, without calling the Hub, unless confirm=true (isError result, error.code CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED). live_traffic: its description tells the model to show the diff, validation result or before/after first. mints_secret: the model agrees owner and scope with the user first.

Fields named by sensitive_output (JSON pointers into the output) are write-once secrets: hubmcp never logs them and returns them only in that result. hubmcp refuses any tool call whose arguments contain a string matching secret_patterns (isError result, error.code SECRET_IN_INPUT; hub_invoke: outcome=refused), without calling the Hub.
Errors from the Hub are returned as tool results with isError=true and the canonical error object, not as protocol errors.
A 202 is reported as outcome=queued, never as success.

forbidden_operations.reason: HTTP DELETE. Deleting stays a manual console action.
Unseal exposes sealed payloads (D6); audited, console only.
Drain and retire take an account out of service.
The request body requires credentials (secret values). Accounts are created in the console or with hubctl until the CCR that makes credentials optional lands.
Credential rotation; console or hubctl only.
Breaker force stops traffic to an account endpoint.
Breaker force; operator decision, console only.
Pause is a kill switch for live traffic.
Resume undoes an operator kill switch.
Revoke irreversibly disables a key (a delete in effect).
Rotation retires the old key; console only.
Rotation retires the old signing secret and mints a new one; console only.

tools.name: hub_list_integrations
tools.title: List integrations
tools.description: List the integrations this API key's tenant can invoke. Each item gives the integration_id (use it in other hub_* tools), the operations it supports with each operation's request_schema (the JSON Schema of the body to send: fields in required are required, the rest optional), its delivery mode (sync returns a result immediately; wait/async may return 'queued'), whether it is interactive, whether it is paused, and whether it moves money or quota (then hub_invoke needs confirm=true and an idempotency_key). Use this first when the user mentions a third-party action and you don't know the integration id.

operations.description: hub-public OperationDescriptor[]: name, description, idempotent, request_schema { body, headers? } (JSON Schema documents).

safety: Read-only.
Output is the caller-facing IntegrationSummary only; no vendor/account/version fields exist in it.

operations.name: default
operations.description: Track a single event for a user.

tools.name: hub_describe_integration
tools.title: Describe an integration
tools.description: Get everything needed to call one integration correctly: its delivery policy (mode, wait window, TTL, what happens when the upstream is down) and, for each operation, its request_schema: the JSON Schema of the body (and of any caller headers it reads). Fields listed in required must be sent; the others are optional. Always call this before hub_invoke or hub_dry_run so you build a body that matches request_schema — a mismatch is rejected with VALIDATION_FAILED. There is no response schema: the result is whatever the integration returns. Fields tagged x-pii hold personal data: only send values the user actually provided.

operations.description: hub-public OperationDescriptor[]: name, description, idempotent, request_schema { body, headers? } (JSON Schema documents).

safety: Read-only.
One caller-API read; it exposes no vendor/account/version.

operations.name: default
operations.description: Track a single event for a user.

tools.name: hub_dry_run
tools.title: Dry-run an integration (developer tool)
tools.description: Show the exact upstream HTTP request the Hub WOULD send for a request body, without sending anything (no side effects, no quota used). Use it to check a body before a real call, or when the user is developing an integration. IMPORTANT: unlike every other tenant tool, the result reveals the upstream request shape (URL, headers, body) with secrets replaced by ***; do not present it to end users as the integration's contract, and never build logic on it — it changes whenever the Hub cuts over. Requires an API key with the dry_run scope; otherwise you get FORBIDDEN.

body.description: Request body matching the operation's request_schema.body (see hub_describe_integration).

headers.description: Caller headers the operation reads, as declared in its request_schema.headers (see hub_describe_integration). hubmcp forwards only header names declared there and refuses the Hub's own headers (Authorization, Idempotency-Key, Prefer, X-Request-Deadline, X-Hub-Session, traceparent); use the dedicated inputs for those.

session.description: X-Hub-Session from step 1 of a multi-step flow.

safety: Documented exception to the no-vendor-leak rule (x-audience: integration-developers).
No upstream call, no queue entry, no idempotency record.
Secrets are redacted by the Hub; hubmcp additionally refuses to output any header value not equal to *** for headers listed in `redacted`.

tools.name: hub_invoke
tools.title: Invoke an integration
tools.description: Call an integration for real with a request body that matches the operation's request_schema. This has real-world effects (events sent, messages delivered, money or quota possibly consumed). Steps: 1) hub_describe_integration to get the request_schema; 2) build the body; 3) call hub_invoke. Always pass an idempotency_key (a stable string per logical action, e.g. 'order-8821-created') so a retry cannot double-send. If the integration has moves_money_or_quota=true you MUST first show the user what will be sent and get explicit approval, then call with confirm=true. Results: outcome=completed gives the integration's result (any JSON; there is no response schema); outcome=queued means accepted but NOT done yet — tell the user and use hub_get_request with the request_id to follow up; outcome=error gives a canonical error (if retryable is true you may retry with the same idempotency_key after retry_after_ms). When pass_through is true the result is the third party's own response, returned unchanged: any 2xx (also 202) is outcome=completed with the third party's status in http_status; on outcome=error with pass_through=true, error is null and result holds the third party's error body with http_status as its status. For interactive (multi-step) integrations, pass the session returned by step 1.

operation.description: Operation name from hub_describe_integration. Omit for single-operation integrations.

body.description: Request body matching the operation's request_schema.body.

headers.description: Caller headers the operation reads, as declared in its request_schema.headers (see hub_describe_integration). hubmcp forwards only header names declared there and refuses the Hub's own headers (Authorization, Idempotency-Key, Prefer, X-Request-Deadline, X-Hub-Session, traceparent); use the dedicated inputs for those.

idempotency_key.description: Strongly recommended; mandatory when moves_money_or_quota is true.

prefer_async.description: Send Prefer: respond-async (accept a queued answer if the upstream is down).

session.description: X-Hub-Session for step 2+ of a multi-step flow.

confirm.description: Must be true for integrations with moves_money_or_quota=true, after the user explicitly approved this exact call.

result.description: Response body when completed: the integration's output, any JSON value (a non-JSON body is given as a string). With pass_through=true and outcome=error, the third party's error body. null otherwise.

pass_through.description: true when the Hub returned the third party's status and body unchanged (X-Hub-Pass-Through: true; the integration has no response transformer).

error.description: Canonical error object (code, message, retryable, retry_after_ms, ...), or a local refusal with code CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED / IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REQUIRED.

safety: Side-effecting. destructiveHint=true so clients prompt the user.

Pre-check: GET integration; if paused, return the error without invoking; if moves_money_or_quota and (confirm != true or no idempotency_key) return outcome=refused, code CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED or IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REQUIRED, without calling the Hub.

Never forwards any header that could select a vendor/account/version (none exist in the contract). hubmcp sends Authorization, Idempotency-Key, Prefer, X-Request-Deadline, X-Hub-Session, traceparent, plus only the caller headers the operation declares in request_schema.headers.
Strips X-Hub-Integration-Version and X-Hub-Served-By from output.
Never auto-retries a non-retryable error; retries a retryable one at most once and only when idempotency_key is set.

tools.name: hub_get_request
tools.title: Get request status
tools.description: Check the status of an earlier hub_invoke by request_id — use it after an outcome=queued. status is one of accepted, in_flight, retry_scheduled, parked (waiting for the upstream to recover), succeeded (result holds the response body), failed or dead_lettered (error holds why), expired (it was not delivered before its TTL). Do not poll in a tight loop: wait at least a few seconds between calls and tell the user it is still pending.

result.description: Response body when succeeded (any JSON value), else null.

safety: Read-only.
Only the calling tenant's requests are visible (others give REQUEST_NOT_FOUND).

tools.name: hub_admin_search_requests
tools.title: Search requests (admin, read-only)
tools.description: Operator tool: search the Hub's request ledger across tenants (or within your tenant scope) by integration, status, error code, vendor, account and time range. Unlike tenant tools, results include vendor_id, account_id and integration version, because this is the control plane. Use it to investigate incidents ('which requests to int_evt_brandA timed out in the last hour?'). The time range must be ≤ 31 days; default to the last hour if the user gives none. Requires HUB_ADMIN_TOKEN.
safety: Read-only; registered only when HUB_ADMIN_TOKEN is set.
Returns no payload bodies (summary rows only); use the console for bodies. Never calls unsealRequest.

tools.name: hub_admin_request_timeline
tools.title: Request audit timeline (admin, read-only)
tools.description: Operator tool: get the full audit timeline of one request — received, validated, resolved (which integration version, vendor, account and transformers were used), transformed, each upstream attempt and response, and the final outcome — plus the attempt list. Payloads follow the integration's audit policy: masked values are hashes, sealed payloads are null (this tool cannot unseal). Use it to explain why a specific request failed. Requires HUB_ADMIN_TOKEN.

include_payloads.description: Include (masked) event payloads; default returns metadata, sha256 and sizes only to save context.

safety: Read-only; registered only when HUB_ADMIN_TOKEN is set.
Never unseals. Masked/sealed policy is enforced by the Hub, not by hubmcp.

tools.name: hub_admin_breaker_states
tools.title: Circuit breaker states (admin, read-only)
tools.description: Operator tool: list circuit breakers per (account, endpoint) with state (closed / open / half_open), whether an operator forced it, failure ratio, when it reopens, and how many requests are parked behind it. Use it to answer 'is vendor X down?' or 'why are requests queued?'. Filter by vendor_id, account_id or state. Requires HUB_ADMIN_TOKEN.
safety: Read-only; registered only when HUB_ADMIN_TOKEN is set.
Never calls force-open / force-close / clear-force.

tools.name: hub_admin_list_tenants
tools.title: List tenants (admin, read-only)
tools.description: Operator tool: list tenants, the identities that teams' services use to call the Hub with API keys. Each row says whether the tenant is disabled, how many integrations it owns and how many active API keys it has. Filter with q. Use it to check whether a tenant already exists before hub_admin_create_tenant. Requires HUB_ADMIN_TOKEN.

q.description: Case-insensitive substring of the id or display name.

safety: Read-only (GET); registered only when HUB_ADMIN_TOKEN is set.

tools.name: hub_admin_get_tenant
tools.title: Get a tenant (admin, read-only)
tools.description: Operator tool: get one tenant (display name, contact, rate limit, disabled flag, counts) and its etag. Call it before hub_admin_update_tenant to show the user the current values and to get the etag for if_match. Requires HUB_ADMIN_TOKEN.

outputSchema.description: hub-admin Tenant. Plus etag (from the ETag header).

etag.description: ETag response header. Pass it as if_match to the matching update tool.

safety: Read-only (GET); registered only when HUB_ADMIN_TOKEN is set.

tools.name: hub_admin_create_tenant
tools.title: Create a tenant (admin)
tools.description: Admin write tool: create a tenant, the identity a team's services use to call the Hub. It starts with no API keys (mint one with hub_admin_create_api_key) and owns no integrations. tenant_id is permanent (3-64 characters: letters, digits, _ and -), so agree on it and the display name with the user first. CONFLICT if it already exists. Needs the admin role: you act as the signed-in user, and the Hub answers FORBIDDEN if their role is lower. reason is required and lands in the change log under the user's identity.

rate_limit.description: Tenant rate limit: rps (requests per second) and burst.

reason.description: Why this change is made, in the user's words (e.g. 'Onboard brand A analytics, OPS-123'). Required. Recorded in the change log under the signed-in user's identity, with ' (via hubmcp)' appended.

safety: Mutating. Registered only when HUB_ADMIN_TOKEN is set and the transport is stdio; acts as the signed-in user. The Hub's RBAC decides (x-required-role: admin); a lower role gets FORBIDDEN as an isError result.
reason is required; the change log records it with the user's identity and the " (via hubmcp)" marker.
Accepts no secret values (no credentials, tokens or signing secrets).
Not idempotent: a repeat gets CONFLICT and changes nothing.

tools.name: hub_admin_update_tenant
tools.title: Update a tenant (admin)
tools.description: Admin write tool: merge-patch a tenant's display_name, description, contact and rate_limit; only the fields you pass change. A rate_limit change applies to the tenant's live traffic within seconds (too low a value throttles every call it makes), so: 1) hub_admin_get_tenant; 2) show the user current and new values; 3) after explicit approval, call with confirm=true and if_match set to the etag. Disabling a tenant is not possible through MCP; it stays a manual console action. Needs the admin role (FORBIDDEN otherwise).

rate_limit.description: Tenant rate limit: rps (requests per second) and burst.

reason.description: Why this change is made, in the user's words (e.g. 'Onboard brand A analytics, OPS-123'). Required. Recorded in the change log under the signed-in user's identity, with ' (via hubmcp)' appended.

if_match.description: The etag returned by the matching hub_admin_get_* tool. Strongly recommended: if the object changed since you read it, the Hub answers PRECONDITION_FAILED and nothing changes (read it again and re-confirm with the user).

confirm.description: Must be true, set only after you showed the user exactly what changes (diff, validation result or before/after values) and they explicitly approved this call. Without it the tool refuses locally with CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED and calls nothing.

safety: Mutating. Registered only when HUB_ADMIN_TOKEN is set and the transport is stdio; acts as the signed-in user. The Hub's RBAC decides (x-required-role: tenant_admin; admin also qualifies); a lower role gets FORBIDDEN as an isError result.
reason is required; the change log records it with the user's identity and the " (via hubmcp)" marker.
requires_confirm=live_traffic: refuses locally (CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED, no Hub call) unless confirm=true.
Never sends disabled (no kill switch through MCP).
Accepts no secret values (no credentials, tokens or signing secrets).

tools.name: hub_admin_create_api_key
tools.title: Create an API key (admin, shows the key once)
tools.description: Admin write tool: mint an API key for a tenant. Scopes: invoke, dry_run, requests_read, each optionally narrowed to one integration as <scope>:<integration_id>; grant only what the user needs. Agree on tenant, scopes and expiry with the user, then call with confirm=true. SENSITIVE OUTPUT: `secret` is the full key, shown exactly once (the Hub keeps only a hash). Give it to the user once, verbatim, and tell them to store it in their secret manager now. Never repeat it later, never put it in another tool call, file, code sample, commit or memory, and never summarise it; afterwards refer to the key by key_id or prefix. If it is lost, the user rotates the key in the console. Needs the admin role (FORBIDDEN otherwise).

description.description: What the key is for, e.g. "orders prod".

reason.description: Why this change is made, in the user's words (e.g. 'Onboard brand A analytics, OPS-123'). Required. Recorded in the change log under the signed-in user's identity, with ' (via hubmcp)' appended.

confirm.description: Must be true, set only after the user explicitly approved minting this secret (owner, scopes or URL, expiry). Without it the tool refuses locally with CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED and calls nothing.

secret.description: SENSITIVE, shown once. Hand to the user verbatim once; never repeat it.

safety: Mutating. Registered only when HUB_ADMIN_TOKEN is set and the transport is stdio; acts as the signed-in user. The Hub's RBAC decides (x-required-role: admin); a lower role gets FORBIDDEN as an isError result.
reason is required; the change log records it with the user's identity and the " (via hubmcp)" marker.
requires_confirm=mints_secret: refuses locally (CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED, no Hub call) unless confirm=true.
sensitive_output /secret: never logged by hubmcp, returned only in this one result; any later tool call whose arguments contain a Hub secret is refused (SECRET_IN_INPUT).
Not idempotent: every call mints a new key.

tools.description: Operator tool: list the third-party vendors registered in the Hub with their auth scheme, regions and endpoint/account counts. Filter with q. Use it before hub_admin_create_vendor to avoid duplicates. Requires HUB_ADMIN_TOKEN.

safety: Read-only (GET); registered only when HUB_ADMIN_TOKEN is set.

tools.description: Operator tool: get one vendor in full (regions, auth scheme, defaults, webhook verification, docs URL, its endpoints, revision) and its etag. Call it before hub_admin_update_vendor: that tool replaces every mutable field, so start from these values. Requires HUB_ADMIN_TOKEN.

safety: Read-only (GET); registered only when HUB_ADMIN_TOKEN is set.

tools.name: hub_admin_create_vendor
tools.title: Create a vendor (admin)
tools.description: Admin write tool: register a third-party vendor: base URL per region, auth scheme (only its shape, e.g. static_headers or bearer; credential values are set per account in the console or with hubctl, never here), optional defaults (per-account rate limit, breaker, health probe) and inbound webhook verification. The Hub only lets traffic out to the declared hosts. Check base URLs against the vendor's current API docs and pass docs_url. Add endpoints next with hub_admin_create_vendor_endpoint. Needs the admin role (FORBIDDEN otherwise).

tools.name: hub_admin_update_vendor
tools.title: Update a vendor (admin)
tools.description: Admin write tool: replace a vendor's mutable fields (display_name, auth_scheme, regions, defaults, webhook_verification, docs_url). It affects every account and integration on this vendor and reaches live traffic with the next config snapshot, so show the user the before/after, and only after explicit approval call with confirm=true and if_match set to the etag. if_match.description: The etag returned by the matching hub_admin_get_* tool. Strongly recommended: if the object changed since you read it, the Hub answers PRECONDITION_FAILED and nothing changes (read it again and re-confirm with the user).

confirm.description: Must be true, set only after you showed the user exactly what changes (diff, validation result or before/after values) and they explicitly approved this call. Without it the tool refuses locally with CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED and calls nothing.

safety: Mutating. Registered only when HUB_ADMIN_TOKEN is set and the transport is stdio; acts as the signed-in user. The Hub's RBAC decides (x-required-role: tenant_admin; admin also qualifies); a lower role gets FORBIDDEN as an isError result.
reason is required; the change log records it with the user's identity and the " (via hubmcp)" marker.
requires_confirm=live_traffic: refuses locally (CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED, no Hub call) unless confirm=true.
Never sends disabled; never rotates or deletes the secret.
Accepts no secret values (no credentials, tokens or signing secrets).

input.reason: Orders callbacks moved to the v2 service
